content.title: Stellantis car production in France set for 11% drop by 2028, sources
content.summary:
STORY: Production at Stellantis' French factories is set to drop by 11% over the next three years.

That's according to company estimates cited by trade unions.

It's part of measures by the world's fourth-largest carmaker to tackle overcapacity.

Trade union sources told Reuters that output at the company's five assembly factories in France is forecast to fall to 587,800 units by 2028.

The sources added that production is expected to decrease at three out of the five factories.

Although they said the forecast may shift depending on EU decisions due on December 10th that are expected to add flexibility to meeting CO2 targets in the bloc.

Stellantis declined to comment.

Earlier this year, the carmaker temporarily stopped production at two plants due to weak demand in Europe.

Data released earlier on Monday showed that Stellantis vehicle registrations in France fell by 5.5% in November.

That brings its market share to just over a quarter - down slightly from the same month last year.

content.title: China Just Took Over Europe's EV Battery Dreams--In Spain's Backyard
content.summary: Spain just fired a shot across Europe's industrial landscape, and the echo could be loud.  Stellantis (NYSE:STLA) and China's CATL have broken ground on a 4.1 billion battery plant in northern Spain, a project that could be seen as Europe leaning on Beijing even as policymakers try to counter China's reach.  Madrid is treating it as a win: Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez's government welcomed the investment despite criticism over CATL's plan to rely on its own staff during the build-out.
